bull_case: Axon AI turns ad buying into a higher-ROI automated allocation system that can move beyond gaming into e-commerce and CTV. Better prediction attracts advertiser spend and more conversion data, reinforcing the system.
bear_case: Recommendation models are contestable by Meta, Google, Amazon and other adtech firms with larger data sets. Axon may be superior execution within existing ad markets rather than a durable industry disruption.
thesis: APP clears the DI threshold on product economics, not market-cap eligibility. Axon appears to be changing advertiser allocation through materially better automated performance, and rapid growth with expanding margins is strong adoption evidence. Expansion into e-commerce and CTV adds optionality. The main limitation is incumbent response: the largest digital-ad platforms have deep data, distribution and AI resources, so APP is a strong self-disruptor rather than an uncontested new-value-chain owner.

evidence.claim: Management identifies Axon AI as the core advertising recommendation system and is investing in further enhancements.
FY2025 revenue grew 70% and H1 2026 revenue grew 56%, while adjusted EBITDA margin expanded above 80%.
evidence.value: Revenue +70% FY25; +56% H1; EBITDA margin 84.2% H1

evidence.claim: Management explicitly targets expansion outside gaming into e-commerce and CTV.
Q3 guidance implies continued sequential growth at roughly 83% adjusted EBITDA margin.

counterevidence: Meta, Google and Amazon possess larger first-party data and distribution systems.
APP remains dependent on third-party mobile and web ecosystems for inventory and attribution.
Public disclosure does not quantify a clean 10x cost/performance advantage for Axon.
E-commerce and CTV are newer expansion areas with less mature economics than gaming.
unknowns: Advertiser ROI uplift versus major alternatives.
Long-run competitive response from hyperscale ad platforms.

uncertainties.rationale: Financial outcomes imply major performance gains, but direct ROI comparisons are limited.
Revenue and margin acceleration show production-scale adoption rather than pilots.
Cross-vertical optionality is large, but incumbents can respond aggressively.

falsifiers: Growth slows without corresponding market saturation while competitors report stronger advertiser ROI.
E-commerce/CTV expansion fails to become material.
Privacy/platform changes erode Axon performance faster than product improvements offset them.

key_kpis.name: Revenue growth
key_kpis.threshold: Sustain material share gains beyond gaming

key_kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA / FCF margin
key_kpis.threshold: High performance monetizes without rising acquisition cost

subscores.rationale: Growth and margin expansion imply a structural improvement in ad-allocation economics.
Adoption is clearly at scale, though detailed cohort metrics are not public.
Multiple expansion paths exist, offset by powerful incumbent responses.
